charts.annotation: Gross pipeline is capacity under development group-wide, well ahead of what is actually installed or under construction -- a funnel, not a forecast.

productionSplit.title: Production: liquids vs gas
productionSplit.content:
Hydrocarbon production split between liquids (crude oil, condensate, NGLs) and natural gas, in thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day (kboe/d), against the Brent benchmark price.

For TotalEnergies SE: gas (increasingly LNG-linked) is now roughly half of production, so realized prices depend on both oil and global gas/LNG markets, not Brent alone.

What to watch:

  • Mix shift toward gas as LNG projects (e.g. Mozambique, Papua LNG) ramp
  • Production growth against Brent -- volume can offset a weak price, or vice versa
  • Only reported split by liquids/gas from FY2017; earlier years show total Production only

lng.title: LNG sales and realized price
lng.content:
LNG sales (million tonnes) and the realized LNG price the company actually captured, which can diverge from spot benchmarks on long-term contracts.

For TotalEnergies SE: TotalEnergies is one of the world's top-five LNG players; this business is a structural growth driver as new liquefaction trains (Mozambique LNG, Papua LNG, Rio Grande LNG, Cameron LNG) come online through the late 2020s.

What to watch:

  • Volume growth from new trains versus price, which is set mostly by Asian/European gas markets
  • Portfolio trading gains/losses layered on top of equity LNG volumes

refiningMargin.title: Refining margin benchmark
refiningMargin.content:
The refining margin benchmark (dollars per tonne) measures the theoretical spread refiners capture between crude input and refined-product output for TotalEnergies' own refinery configuration.

For TotalEnergies SE: the company has changed its disclosed benchmark over time as its refinery fleet and the products it indexes against evolved: TRCV through FY2008, ERMI FY2009-FY2016, MCV FY2017-FY2022, and ERM from FY2023. These are sequential proxies for the same underlying economics, not four margins coexisting -- only one is populated in any given year.

What to watch:

  • Margin direction, not the absolute benchmark label, when comparing across the name changes
  • Refining margin versus Refining & Chemicals segment results -- utilization and product mix also matter

renewableCapacity.title: Renewable power capacity
renewableCapacity.content:
Net installed capacity (gigawatts) that is actually generating, under construction capacity committed but not yet operating, and the much larger gross pipeline of projects under development group-wide (before co-investor dilution and before projects are dropped).

For TotalEnergies SE: Integrated Power is the company's fourth growth pillar alongside LNG, upstream and downstream; the gap between gross pipeline and installed capacity shows how much of the renewables story is still a funnel rather than cash flow.

What to watch:

  • Installed capacity growth converting into Integrated Power segment earnings, not just pipeline growth
  • Attrition between gross pipeline and what actually reaches construction

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For TotalEnergies SE: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For TotalEnergies SE: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For TotalEnergies SE: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For TotalEnergies SE: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For TotalEnergies SE: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For TotalEnergies SE: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For TotalEnergies SE: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For TotalEnergies SE: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For TotalEnergies SE: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For TotalEnergies SE: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
